Early signal•Blood · Amyloid PET · p-tau217

Pooled cohorts linked very high p-tau217 to 38% five-year progression risk in unimpaired adults

Peer-reviewed pooled longitudinal cohort study · Source date July 14, 2026

Among 2,684 selected cognitively unimpaired participants, very high p-tau217 was associated with 38% five-year absolute risk of cognitive impairment, but the authors cautioned against individual prognosis in unselected populations.

Key quantitative result: 478 participants progressed to cognitive impairment.

Added September 4, 2026 · DOI:10.1001/jama.2026.12556

Read full brief

Thirty-second field brief

The study provides absolute rather than only relative risk, which is useful for prevention-trial planning. It does not justify routine testing of asymptomatic people: cohorts were selected, assay values were standardized within study, and longer-horizon estimates were sparse.

Study design

Harmonized analysis of 2,684 cognitively unimpaired participants across six North American, Japanese, and Australian cohorts; median follow-up 5.4 years and maximum 13.5 years.

Key quantitative results

  • 478 participants progressed to cognitive impairment.
  • Per 1-SD higher baseline p-tau217, HR 1.38 (95% CI, 1.30–1.46); adjusted for amyloid PET Centiloids, HR 1.32 (1.24–1.41).
  • Five-year absolute risk was 24% (95% CI, 20%–28%) for high and 38% (33%–43%) for very high p-tau217.
  • Very-high group annualized PACC change was −0.07 units/year versus +0.03 in the low group.

What changed

The report translated p-tau217 into time-specific absolute progression risk across multiple cohorts.

Strength of evidence

Moderate prognostic evidence with multicohort consistency; clinical utility and calibration in unselected care populations remain unknown.

Clinical significance

Most people in the very-high group did not progress within five years. A high result is not a diagnosis or a deterministic forecast.

Field medical relevance

Expect questions from clinicians and researchers about screening, counseling, and prevention-trial enrollment. Keep research prognosis separate from approved diagnostic intended use.

Likely external questions

Should asymptomatic adults get p-tau217 testing?
Not on this evidence. The study calls for validation in unselected populations and does not establish a care pathway or benefit from disclosure.
Does 38% mean a person has a 38% personal risk?
It is a group estimate in selected cohorts, not a fully calibrated individual prediction.
Does p-tau217 add beyond amyloid PET?
The association persisted after Centiloid adjustment, but incremental decision value and utility were not tested.

Important limitations

  • Selected research and trial cohorts
  • Within-cohort standardization limits universal thresholds
  • Sparse 10-year data
  • Outcome definitions varied by cohort
  • No disclosure-impact trial

Quanterix or platform relevance

Cross-assay harmonization by SD does not make concentrations or cutoffs interchangeable across platforms.

Access or reimbursement relevance

No evidence supports payer coverage for asymptomatic prognostic testing; downstream counseling and confirmatory testing could be substantial.

Source and citation

Open primary source · DOI

Buckley RF, Townsend DL, Birkenbihl CJ, et al. Prognostic value of blood-based p-tau217 levels for progression to cognitive impairment. JAMA. Published online July 14, 2026. doi:10.1001/jama.2026.12556.
